title: A novelist who picks a character name from a tradition the audience recognizes inherits the audience's expectations before the character acts
body:
- Names like Malachi or Amos carry tonal weight when an audience recognizes their association with scriptural gravitas or direct prophetic tradition
- Different biblical names carry different specific associations — Amos as social justice prophet, Malachi as covenant messenger — and the choice between them narrows what kind of authority the character is read as having
- Choosing a biblical name over a historical-figure name determines whether the character's authority reads as primarily theological or culturally rooted
- Case: Amos and Malachi — the first signals a social justice prophet, the second a covenant messenger, and the audience receives those associations before the character acts.
conversion: none — standing condition: the novelist gains characterization the character has not performed, and the audience's expectations are set before the character provides any evidence
